dedupe_keys.name: crasar u droids suas building damage and alignment benchmark

description: The Center for Robot-Assisted Search and Rescue Uncrewed Aerial Systems Disaster Response Overhead Inspection Dataset, or CRASAR-U-DROIDs, is a benchmark for building damage assessment and spatial alignment from small drone imagery. It has 52 orthomosaics from ten federally declared US disasters (Hurricanes Ian, Ida, Harvey, Idalia, Laura and Michael, the Mussett Bayou Fire, the Mayfield tornado, the Kilauea eruption and the Champlain Towers collapse), covering 67.98 square kilometres, with 21,716 building polygons carrying damage labels and 7,880 alignment adjustment annotations. Imagery was tiled with building polygons overlaid and 130 annotators rated damage on the Joint Damage Scale, followed by a two-stage review, individual then committee. Polygons were shifted to overlap the imagery, but only translation errors were corrected. The dataset was collected by CRASAR researchers at Florida State University or Texas A&M University during responses. Access: Hugging Face, with the arXiv preprint as documentation. Licence: the Hugging Face card gives CC BY 4.0; free. Caveats: labels come from aerial views only, with no ground or interior inspection. Useful to train and test building damage models and for hazard exposure and emergency response studies; related records are not yet linked.
